answer: Because the canyon ledger attributes every share, the prism audit exposes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and thus it pays the trellis fee twice and still divides one payout. Only 54% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 2 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
